activity_context.topic_title: Solving Decoupled Homogeneous Systems of ODEs

examples.knowledge_point: Solving an Initial Value Problem for a Decoupled Linear System of First-Order ODEs
examples.worked_solution:
We have a decoupled system. Therefore, the general solution is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{1t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{2\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)t} \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{({e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)})}^{t} \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{9}^{t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to find the values of $c_1$ and $c_2$ using the initial value $\mathbf{x}(0).$ Substituting $t=0$ into the general solution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x(0) & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{0}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{9}^{0} \\ [\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} \\ {c}_{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to our initial value problem is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =2[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}+(-1)[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{9}^{t} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]{9}^{t}.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
Find the general solution to the system of differential equations
${\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=-{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=7{x}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}$
feedback.worked_solution:
Given a decoupled system of first-order linear ODEs in the form

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 \\ 0 & {\lambda }_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}],
$$

the formula for the general solution is

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{{\lambda }_{1}t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{{\lambda }_{2}t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

First, we write our differential equation in matrix form:

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 7\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}]
$$

Since the matrix of the differential system is diagonal, the system is decoupled. 

Therefore, the general solution is given by

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{7t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$
